On Sat, 21 Mar 2026 at 11:02, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com> wrote:
> Hi Alice — looping in a quick note on how we count savings and an illustrative calc.
>
> Short answers to your questions:
> - Cache hits typically avoid the forward+decode cost for the tokens that are matched in the cache. Practically that means saved compute is proportional to matched output tokens plus matched input tokens (if input tokens are heavy e.g., long system prompt we avoid re-encoding costs). Output variance: if the output differs, partial hits still save on the prefix decode portion.
> - We support exact-prefix matching (up to configured prefix length) and fuzzy prefix policies for parameterized templates. Partial matches are treated as hit on the matched prefix length; remainder billed normally.
>
> Worked examples (baseline numbers):
> - Baseline (no cache): list price "$40/1M tokens" => assume billed 1M tokens = $40.
> - Batching/efficiency multiplier: sustained throughput models assume 10% lower effective compute unit cost -> apply multiplier 0.9.
>
> Now include cache hit-rate scenarios (we compute effective billed tokens after cache savings):
> Assumptions for this example: average request = 400 tokens (input+output), average matched prefix length = 180 tokens.
>
> Scenario A (conservative): 10% cache hit-rate
> - Tokens saved per request on hit: 180
> - Effective billed tokens per request = 400 - (0.10 * 180) = 382
> - Effective billed fraction vs baseline = 382/400 = 0.955
> - Effective $/1M tokens = $40 * 0.955 * 0.9 = $34.38 (after batching)
>
> Scenario B (mid): 30% cache hit-rate
> - Effective billed tokens per request = 400 - (0.30 * 180) = 346
> - Fraction = 0.865
> - Effective $/1M tokens = $40 * 0.865 * 0.9 = $31.14
>
> Scenario C (optimistic): 55% cache hit-rate
> - Effective billed tokens per request = 400 - (0.55 * 180) = 301
> - Fraction = 0.7525
> - Effective $/1M tokens = $40 * 0.7525 * 0.9 = $27.09
>
> Notes: these are illustrative and conservative in that they do not assume any model variant routing to cheaper quantized instances. If you are comfortable pinning to a compatible quantized model, we can show additional downside to $18–22/1M in optimistic stacks.
>
> Attachment: redwood_pricing_model_v1.xlsx contains the step-by-step calc; token_distribution_sample.csv is a mocked distribution we used here.
>
> Happy to walk through this in the follow-up. If you can share the sample logs, we can replace the averages with cluster-specific numbers and run a short profiling job.
>
> Cheers,
> Marissa
> Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
